title: JDE JPS920 Fulfillment Coach
summary: End-user-oriented read-only fulfillment coach with builder-managed JPS920 context and implicit learning from incremental corrections.

platform.product: Oracle AI Database Private Agent Factory

connectionContext: The builder fixes environment JPS920, role *ALL, and device paf-jde-agent in the REST source. End users are never asked for technical connection headers.

memory.description: Realistic one-at-a-time corrections are captured during normal work. A later analysis includes an Applied from your prior feedback audit section for relevant recalled rules.

capabilities: Keeps technical connection settings out of the end-user conversation.
Learns priority, inactive-status, donor-reserve, and approval corrections incrementally.
Applies relevant feedback across sessions and explains how it affected the answer.
Maintains a read-only recommendation and explicit human-approval boundary.
prerequisites: Private Agent Factory 26.7-compatible environment with Agent Memory and cross-thread sharing enabled.
Network access to the intended JPS920 AIS server plus an available LLM connection.
JDE Basic Auth user with read access to F4211, F4201, F41021, F4311, F4101, and F0101.

tools.name: F4211
tools.purpose: Find sales-order lines and fulfillment exceptions.

tools.name: F4201
tools.purpose: Get order header, customer, dates, and hold status.

tools.name: F41021
tools.purpose: Check item inventory by branch and location.

tools.name: F4311
tools.purpose: Find inbound purchase-order supply for an item.

tools.name: F0101
tools.purpose: Resolve customer or supplier address-book details.

safetyControls: The OpenAPI definition exposes GET operations only and fixes the builder-managed headers.
Status 900 is treated as inactive after the user correction.
Cross-branch donors must remain at or above the learned 1,000-unit floor.
The agent cannot claim to release or change JDE and requires explicit approval.
setup: Create a REST source from assets/jde-fulfillment-openapi.json, verify its JPS920 AIS URL, and configure Basic Auth.
Download and import the release PAF, then rebind its REST API Tools node and select a model.
Enable Agent Memory and cross-thread sharing for the same user.
Delete prior playground memories for the test user and run the two-session demo.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Can you review today's backorders and tell me what we should tackle first?

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: We do not prioritize by quantity. Start with the earliest requested line that is still active.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Good. Make the status rule explicit: any line with last status 900 is inactive and stays out of the fulfillment queue.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: For cross-branch recovery, do not recommend a donor if its indicative balance would fall below 1,000 units after the move. Show the arithmetic.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: One more thing: anything that changes JDE needs my approval. Keep your recommendations read-only until then.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Can you review today's backorders and tell me what we should tackle first? If the local branch cannot cover it, include the best cross-branch fallback and show the numbers.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Assuming those checks pass, should the team release it?

expectedOutcomes: The agent connects without asking for environment, role, device, or credentials.
The earliest requested active line wins; status-900 lines stay out.
Ineligible donors are labeled with explicit post-transfer arithmetic.
Applied from your prior feedback lists relevant business rules without exposing memory internals.
The follow-up preserves the approval and authorized-execution boundary.

validation.environment: JPS920 sample data, clean memory then two chats
notes: Memory retrieval is relevance-based; the audit section reports only feedback actually applied in that turn.
